newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-WIMBLEDON OUTLOOK BRIGHTER DESPITE RAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WIMBLEDON OUTLOOK BRIGHTER DESPITE RAIN.

text.p: The threat of the first completely washed-out day at Wimbledon for five years was receding on Wednesday despite heavy morning rain.
Forecasters suggested the weather would improve sufficiently to allow some play in the afternoon, although rain was still falling at the scheduled noon start time.

Showers permitted only 16 matches to be completed on Monday's opening day, but a full day's play on Tuesday has at least given tournament referee Alan Mills some breathing space, despite predictions of more showers for the rest of the week.

In 1992 the second Friday was washed out, forcing the tournament to be extended into the Monday of the following week, but the wettest championships in recent memory were in 1991 when play took place on the middle Sunday for the first time.
Play was also extended into a third week last year when the women's and mixed doubles finals were delayed until the Monday.
If the weather does relent, defending champion Richard Krajicek will be among the early starters in a second round match against Romania's Andrei Pavel.
British fans are also awaiting their favourites Tim Henman and Greg Rusedski, who are scheduled to play later in the day.
